name: Jacqueline Ueda
life: “I still remember admitting I felt sick halfway through a school boat trip.” On Friday, near the bank steps, Jacqueline takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I put in an offer and withdrew it when my son said he gets seasick every trip.
appearance: Jacqueline is easy to recognize by close-cropped dark curls and a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Usually dressed in a striped cotton shirt with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf, Jacqueline grins on one side while the eyes stay serious when listening.
personality: Jacqueline gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Jacqueline privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To let the son decline the sailing life.
family: Carol Reed is Jacqueline’s older cousin. Jacqueline brings a spare shopping bag. Carol chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A widow bids again*, Carol says, “I can put my pension into the joint offer. My husband says choosing the city over our kids needs both our signatures.”
connections: Cara Mann. A withdrawn bidder and a canvas buyer discover how little boat each actually wanted.

reactions.response: Jacqueline asks both owners which decision has actually been made.

reactions.response: Jacqueline lets the child choose whether to stand by the door or sit beside the window while another adult gets help.
